# postcss-sketchify

> postcss-sketchify is a PostCSS plugin that turns the borders, fills and underlines of plain CSS into hand-drawn SVG sketches at build time, without changing layout.

Every element keeps its position and size: borders keep their width and style, only their colour turns transparent and a hand-drawn SVG takes its place through `border-image`. There is no JavaScript at runtime; the drawings are written into the CSS, and the same CSS always gives the same output. It is tested in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. MIT licensed, Node 20 or later.

## Install and use

```sh
npm install --save-dev postcss-sketchify postcss
```

```js
// postcss.config.js (Vite, Next.js, webpack and Parcel read it)
import sketchify from 'postcss-sketchify';
export default { plugins: [sketchify({ roughness: 'normal' })] };
```

Without a build tool: `npx sketchify style.css -o style.sketch.css` (also `-d <folder>`, `--watch`, standard input to standard output).

## What gets drawn

- `border` on all four sides (solid, px width, one colour, radius up to 32px): a hand-drawn box.
- A single side (`border-bottom`) or `hr { border-top: … }`: a hand-drawn line reaching both ends.
- `text-decoration: underline` on inline elements: a hand-drawn line under each line of text.
- `--sketch-fill: rough | marker | hatch` next to a `background-color`: a rough fill, a highlighter swipe or hatching.
- `:hover`, `:focus`, modifiers (`.btn.btn--primary`), `@media` rules and `prefers-color-scheme: dark` themes keep the same shape in their own colour.
- `@sketchify base;` adds hand-drawn defaults for form controls, buttons, links and `hr`, which your own styles always override.

## Options

- `roughness`: `'subtle'`, `'normal'` (default), `'messy'` or a number.
- `hatch`: `'fine'`, `'normal'` (default), `'bold'` or your own numbers.
- `base`: colours for `@sketchify base`.
- `quiet`: warning kinds to leave out.
- `budget`: size warning threshold, `{ gzip: 30 }` KB by default.
- Per rule: `--sketch: off` leaves a rule as written; `--sketch-size: 240 160` gives an element's size for an exact hatch.

## Limits

- Colours must be known at build time: `currentColor`, a border without a colour, or a variable changed by a class is an error.
- Meant for your own CSS; frameworks like Bootstrap or Pico, which theme through classes and attributes, mostly end in errors.
- Dashed or dotted borders, borders with different colours per side and radii over 32px stay as plain CSS, with a warning.
- Drawings add size to the CSS, typically 2–11 KB gzip per page.
- Firefox: when a hover swaps the drawing, the border can go blank for one frame.
